# Lab 7.4: Data Transfer Service: Amazon S3 / Azure Blob

## What We Are Going to Do
Load files from Amazon S3 (or Azure Blob Storage) into BigQuery on a schedule. You need an AWS or Azure account with a small test bucket.

## Steps

1. **Prepare the other cloud.** In AWS, create a bucket such as `my-bq-lab-bucket`, upload `sales_1.csv` from Lab 7.3, and create an IAM user with **AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess**. Note the access key and secret.

2. **[SQL] Create the destination table.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE TABLE lab07.sales_s3 (sale_id INT64, city STRING, amount NUMERIC, sale_date DATE);</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[Console] Create the transfer.** **Pipelines and connections → Create → Load data → Amazon S3**:
   - **Destination table**: `sales_s3`
   - **Amazon S3 URI**: `s3://my-bq-lab-bucket/*.csv`
   - **Access key ID / Secret access key**: from step 1
   - **File format**: CSV, header rows to skip: 1

4. **[CLI] The same with bq.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq mk --transfer_config --data_source=amazon_s3 --target_dataset=lab07 \
  --display_name=s3_sales --params='{
    "data_path": "s3://my-bq-lab-bucket/*.csv",
    "destination_table_name_template": "sales_s3",
    "access_key_id": "AKIA...",
    "secret_access_key": "....",
    "file_format": "CSV",
    "skip_leading_rows": "1"
  }'</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   For Azure, use `--data_source=azure_blob_storage` with the storage account, container and SAS token.

5. **[SQL] Check and clean up.**

   Delete the transfer and the AWS key when done. AWS charges for data leaving S3.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Source | S3 or Azure Blob, on a schedule |
| Auth | Access keys (S3) or SAS token (Azure) |
| Cost | Other-cloud egress fees |
| Clean-up | Delete transfer and keys |
